title: Embedding Reliability Labs: cross-functional action plan and SLO experiment roadmap
content:
Purpose and intent:

This is an operational-first action plan for running an "Embedding Reliability Labs" program — a series of short cross-functional sprints that pair product/infra/serving/runtime/console teams with SRE to validate SLOs, iterate on detection/auto-remediation, and exercise graceful degradation paths for inference workloads. The goal is to create repeatable, measurable experiments that (a) prove SLO targets for critical routes, (b) surface weakest links in the serving stack, and (c) leave durable artifacts (dashboards, runbooks, rollout knobs) for product teams.

Why now:
- Multiple product teams are planning heavy LLM rollouts in H1 2027; we need consistent SLOs for latency and availability across hosted and dedicated tiers.
- Several postmortems highlighted gaps in fallback behavior for model variants and region failover.
- We want to reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) for token-level regressions and accelerate safe canary-to-production rollouts.

Success criteria (what "done" looks like):
- 3 production routes (chat-gen, embeddings, rerank) instrumented with aligned SLO definitions and dashboards.
- Two automated remediation playbooks implemented (cache/kv warming and routing fallback to cheaper/older model) and exercised in controlled experiments.
- Clear SLA->SLO translation doc for customers (one-pager) and internal handshake with GTM.
- Training session + tabletop runbook drill delivered to oncall rotation and 2 product teams.
- SLO alert noise reduced by 30% through signal tuning and synthetic test coverage.

High-level approach and phases:
Phase 0: Kickoff + alignment (2 weeks)
- Stakeholder readouts: product owners, infra, serving runtime, console, client SDK, CS/Support.
- Collect current SLAs/expectations and existing metrics (p99 latency, error rate, token-throughput, cold-start time).
- Quick inventory of available signals (trace spans, Redwood Console traces, token cost telemetry).
- Deliverable: Program charter + prioritized route list.

Phase 1: Baseline instrumentation and synthetic canaries (4 weeks)
- Implement lightweight SLO exporters where missing: route-level p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx/error-class, abort-rate, cold-start percent for model pools.
- Add synthetic traffic harness (varying payload size + sequence length distributions) in staging and one preprod region.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO panel, upstream/downstream dependency waterfall (model load, queue time, kernel latency).
- Deliverable: Baseline dashboard + observability checklist.

Phase 2: Focused experiments (6 weeks, parallel experiments)
Experiment A: Batching and latency trade-offs
- Owners: serving-runtime + infra + product chat team.
- Hypothesis: Dynamic batching improvements + adaptive max_batch_size yields 20% p95 latency improvement with <3% throughput loss.
- Plan: A/B compare two batching profiles in dedicated pool; measure tail latency, token-efficiency, and error amplifications.
- Playbook: Fall back to conservative batching profile if p99 increases >10% or error > threshold.

Experiment B: KV/prefix cache warm-up and regression detection
- Owners: optimize + srep + console.
- Hypothesis: Pre-warming KV cache for top-20 prefixes reduces p95 by X and reduces cold-start variance.
- Plan: Synthetic sequences with interleaving cold/hot hits, enable pre-warm daemon in subset of nodes. Measure cache hit rate and tail latencies.

Experiment C: Model variant graceful degradation
- Owners: model-onboarding + serving-runtime + product embeddings.
- Hypothesis: Policy routing to quantized fallback model keeps latency SLOs while maintaining acceptable output quality for 90% of requests.
- Plan: Controlled rollout: 5% traffic to fallback with human eval set; monitor embedding distance drift and reranking accuracy metrics.

Phase 3: Runbookization and automation (4 weeks)
- Convert experiment lessons into operational runbooks: detection thresholds, automated routing switch, KV rehydrate steps, escalation matrix.
- Implement two remediation automations in staging: (1) automatic routing fallback triggered by queue-time threshold; (2) preemptive scale-up for sustained token-throughput spikes.
- Deliverable: Runbooks checked into repo + automated playbook tests.

Phase 4: Training + tabletop + customer comms (2 weeks)
- Tabletop: simulate a degradation (region outage + model cache warm-up failure) and run through runbook. Capture gaps.
- Training: 90-minute session for oncall and product owners.
- Customer-facing one-pager: SLOs explained + what to expect during incidents.

Roles and RACI (top-level):
- Program Lead: Asha Kapoor (SRE) — overall coordination, stakeholder alignment, milestone tracking.
- Experiment Leads: Miguel Torres (serving-runtime), Sara Li (console/observability), Evan Brooks (product chat), Priya Shah (model-onboarding).
- Infra SME: Tomas Jensen (autoscaler/capacity) — capacity planning and burst tests.
- Eval/Quality SME: Nina Park — human evals for model fallback experiments.
- Support Liaison: Kelsey Rhee — incident comms and CS FAQ drafts.

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30m sync (Mon 11:00) — quick blockers and milestone updates.
- #reliability-labs Slack channel for async updates and experiment logs.
- Biweekly stakeholder demo (15–30m) to Engineering leadership and product.

Risk register and mitigations (short form):
- Risk: Fallback model causes quality regressions. Mitigation: human eval gate + automatic rollback threshold by embedding-distance drift.
- Risk: Synthetic canaries not representative. Mitigation: use production-sampled traces to seed synthetic harness and vary payload distributions.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from naive SLOs. Mitigation: windowed aggregation and alert burn-in period before paging.

Measurement plan and metrics:
- SLOs (examples we will test/define):
  - chat-gen latency SLO: 99% requests under X ms for prompt length Y.
  - embeddings SLO: 99.9% success rate and p95 latency under Z ms for singleton calls.
  - rerank SLO: end-to-end latency p99 under W ms and error rate < 0.1%.
- Operational metrics: cache hit rate, queue_time, model_load_ms, batch_size_distribution, token-throughput, cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Quality metrics (for fallback experiments): embedding distance drift, nDCG for rerank sample set, human accept rate.

Artifacts to produce (concrete):
- SLO definition doc + examples per route (yaml snippets for Redwood Console ingestion).
- Dashboards: per-route SLO dashboard, dependency waterfall, experiment A/B comparison views.
- Runbooks: detection -> remediation -> escalation with playbook test cases.
- Synthetic harness repo with seed traces and config profiles.
- One-pager SLO->SLA translation for GTM.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need agreement with product on what "acceptable" quality degradation looks like for fallback; schedule joint session with product PMs next Wed.
- Confirm which model variants are approval-ready for fallback (Priya to list).
- Check telemetry retention policy for token-level traces — may need extended retention for experiments (ENG-OPS ticket).
- Who owns the final communication to customers? (Kelsey + Product comms).

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Asha: finalize charter and send calendar invites for weekly sync (by EOD Fri).
- Miguel: prototype synthetic harness scaffolding and post PR for review (target 5 working days).
- Sara: build initial dashboard skeleton in Redwood Console and link sample traces.
- Evan: pick 2 production chat routes as candidates and prepare traffic characteristics export.

Appendix: quick experiment checklist (for each experiment)
- clear hypothesis stated
- owner and experiment lead named
- preflight telemetry available in staging
- canary percent plan and rollback thresholds documented
- human eval plan (if quality affected)
- runbook snippet and test case committed

Retention + handoff:
- After runbookization, each artifact will be owned by an operational owner (SRE steward) and reviewed every quarter.
- Any experiment that becomes default behavior must have a follow-up cost review (Optimize) to ensure unit economics remain acceptable.

Notes on tone: this doc is intentionally pragmatic — half runbook, half experiment plan. Expect iterations and short drafts. Leave early-stage decisions as TODOs rather than making unilateral changes.
